summary: The one-file corrective diff (e07f8a94, packages/node/src/v3-live.ts only) is well-formed and closes three of the four rejected-GREEN blocking findings cleanly: isControlOperation is now profile-gated so creator-trusted-v1 join/causalJoin again reach reservation, sink delivery, journal/recovery acceptance and the blueprint fold (legacy consumers 26/26, including phase-3f-b frontier-reduction and chat-zone causal-join); the settlement issued/outbox cross-read is restored for every profile (5655-5666); the terminal requireTerminalAuthorization && terminalTransactionStarted branch again precedes the generic issuance outcome-unknown return (6431-6440) without weakening nonterminal handling; issueAuthorFence now captures the durable plan through copySettlementPlan (an already-public f5b0s export, so no API/dependency widening) and fails closed on null, malformed, accessor-bearing, extra-key, non-array-entries and wrong-scope plans via plan === undefined; and the sequence-zero exclusion again requires crossSource !== undefined while activationVertexDigest, which is only ever assigned on the cross-object branch (5331), keeps genuine cross-object activation vertices excluded. The RED is mechanically causal (39 selected / 25 passed / 14 failed with zero module, export or setup errors; Phase-3g 13/1), the publishState fixture correction at 9a4b35f4 is correct because the response only carries publishState on the cross-object branch (7000-7010), and the stale-dist diagnostic is honestly retained and correctly explained by dist-identity.txt (dist mtime 00:41 predates the 06:41 source), followed by rebuild, built-shape audit, unchanged replacement title, 64/64 shared consumers and a detached built-child pass. It nevertheless blocks on one item: the diff also adds an exemption that changes frozen creator-trusted-v1 behavior beyond the prescribed repair, and the retained Phase-3g assertions that encoded the frozen behavior were rewritten to bless it rather than production being restored. No stop-rule contradiction on contiguity, device-local plan authority or anchor fencing was found, and no retired grammar or global floor is implied by the required repair.

findings.title: rebaseIntents exemption changes frozen creator-trusted-v1 behavior for displaced join/causalJoin, and the retained Phase-3g assertions that pinned the old behavior were rewritten to match
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6798-6807. The added conjuncts `action !== "causalJoin" && action !== "join"` sit inside a disjunct already guarded by `settlementProfileFor(payload.trust.trust.profileId) !== "v1"`, and under the settlement profile the first disjunct `isControlOperation(sourceOperation, profileId)` already returns `[]` for both actions (3502-3507). The exemption is therefore inert under creator-trusted-settlement-v1 and changes only legacy. Parent 504ca351:6435 was `if (typeof action === "string" && isReservedBatchAction(action)) return ObjectFreeze([]);` and RESERVED_BATCH_ACTIONS (231-237) contains "causalJoin" and "join", so legacy displaced join/causalJoin rows returned `intents: []`. That was not stale: tests/phase-3g-v3-rebase-outbox-red.test.ts asserted `intents: []` plus `completion: {kind:"published", ok:true}` for the legacy "structural" (causalJoin) source since 5d432e7b (2026-08-21) and passed inside the rejected GREEN's own 87/87 retained run (.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0b-green-93585bf3/commands.md:22). The slice's own diagnostic confirms it: .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0b-red-9a4b35f4/diagnostic-values.json:3-13 records legacyJoin returning `intents: []` and the README calls that "incorrectly empty". The frozen expectations were then rewritten by tests-only commits c77f8a1f (`intents: []` -> a causalJoin intent), 4543b957 (operationCount/operationIndex pin) and 6e542c3d (`completion` `{kind:"published",ok:true}` -> `toBeUndefined()`); .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0b-red-c77f8a1f/README.md:4-6 labels the parent expectation "stale" with no cited authority. This contradicts the accepted design's frozen constraint at .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0r-design-3a156aca/design.md:548 ("creator-trusted-v1 behavior byte-for-byte unchanged") and exceeds the rejected review's prescribed repair, which asked only to gate isControlOperation so legacy paths "keep pre-GREEN behavior" (.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0b-review-9b02f9c2/opus/verdict.json, P0 repair). No waiver of design.md:548 is recorded in any f5b0b evidence root. The final GREEN evidence characterizes the result as retention rather than change: .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0b-green-e07f8a94/matrix.md:5 ("legacy application intents retained") and :12 ("Application-visible causalJoin remains pending; it is not silently retired").
findings.failure_scenario: A creator-trusted-v1 (or creator-author-authorization-v1) room with a displaced own `join` row — the exact shape used as the roster bootstrapOperation in examples/grid/src/v3-zone.ts and examples/v3-chat/src/index.ts — calls readRebaseOutbox after a close. On the parent and on the rejected GREEN it received `source.intents: []` and retired the row through completeRebaseSource (the Phase-3g fixture path at tests/fixtures/phase-3g/rebase-outbox-fixture.ts:1118-1129 is driven exactly by `intents.length === 0`). On e07f8a94 the same room now receives a re-issuable `{action:"join", ...}` intent, the completeRebaseSource retirement branch is never taken, and the room's rebase loop re-issues a structural operation as an ordinary application vertex (accepted by issueLocal at 6644-6701). The public readRebaseOutbox contract and the room-side rebase/retirement flow for the frozen legacy profile therefore differ from the parent commit, and the retained gate that would have caught it now asserts the new behavior.
findings.required_action: Either (a) drop `action !== "causalJoin" && action !== "join"` from packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6803-6804 so legacy returns ObjectFreeze([]) exactly as parent 504ca351:6435 did, revert the two rewritten Phase-3g assertions (tests/phase-3g-v3-rebase-outbox-red.test.ts:78-89 back to `intents: []` and `completion: {kind:"published", ok:true}`), drop or re-scope the corrective test at tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b0b-node-corrective-red.test.ts:54-68 to the settlement profile, and re-record RED/GREEN; or (b) if the change to legacy is intended, stop and obtain an explicit recorded user waiver amending design.md:548, record it in the f5b0b evidence with the room-side consequence analysis, and hand the completeRebaseSource/re-issue consequence to f5b0c before landing. Do not close f5b0b on the current evidence, which presents the change as retention.

findings.title: Legacy non-terminal ISSUANCE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN now returns issuance-rejected where the parent returned admission-rejected, with no legacy control
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6438-6445 versus parent 504ca351:6144-6148. When the signature was already produced (`signerResolved === true`) and a non-terminal transactIssue throws `{code:"ISSUANCE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN"}`, the parent returned `localIssueFailure("admission-rejected", "v3 local issue signature was not admitted")`; the new branch returns `internalLocalIssueFailure("issuance-rejected", "v3 local issue transaction outcome is unknown")` first. Admission is halted identically (6428-6430, unchanged from parent), so the safety posture is the same, but the caller-visible `kind` differs under creator-trusted-v1. The reorder itself was prescribed by the prior review; the kind change rides along from the rejected GREEN and no test in the retained, focused or legacy-consumer sets asserts either message.
findings.failure_scenario: A legacy room whose durable issuance store reports an ambiguous outcome on an ordinary application issue now surfaces `kind: "issuance-rejected"` where the parent surfaced `kind: "admission-rejected"`; a legacy caller branching on `kind` takes a different path for the same underlying condition.
findings.required_action: Record this legacy-visible kind change explicitly in the f5b0b evidence (it is currently undisclosed in source-audit.txt and matrix.md), and add one legacy control asserting the ambiguous non-terminal outcome kind when the ambiguous-outcome path is next touched.

findings.title: readSettlementSources still supplies no verified frontier, so terminal/old-incarnation suppression is unreachable in production
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:8644-8650 calls `readRebaseOutbox(registration, true, settlementFrontier)` with `settlementFrontier` undefined at the only production call site (8095), so the `settlementOwnRowClass` terminal/old-incarnation `continue` at 6902-6911 never executes outside tests. This is the already-acknowledged authenticated-frontier-threading gap and matches the disposition recorded at .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0b-review-9b02f9c2/review-ledger.md:34-36; the in-file comment at 8648 states it honestly.
findings.failure_scenario: Until the checkpoint owner threads the verified frontier, a settlement drain retains every authenticated own row rather than dropping rows classified terminal or old-incarnation, so plan building sees candidates the design (design.md:198-203) would have excluded.
findings.required_action: Confirm the existing f5b0c/f5b ownership at slice open and thread the authenticated checkpoint frontier into readSettlementSources; no action inside f5b0b.
